title: The cube is the first power sum needing the middle symmetric function
content: Newton's identities express the power sums $p_k = \sum_i \lambda_i^k$ through the elementary symmetric functions $e_j$: $p_1 = e_1$, $p_2 = e_1^2 - 2e_2$, $p_3 = e_1^3 - 3e_1 e_2 + 3e_3$. The sibling entry settled $p_2$ for $2\times2$ matrices, where $e_2$ is just the determinant — the *top* symmetric function — so only the two extreme invariants (trace and det) appear. The cube $p_3$ in dimension three is the first power sum whose expansion involves the **middle** symmetric function $e_2$ = sum of principal $2\times2$ minors, an invariant that is neither trace nor determinant. That is what makes this case qualitatively harder than the square.
mathContext: $p_3 = e_1^3 - 3e_1 e_2 + 3e_3$; $e_2$ is the genuinely intermediate symmetric function.

title: e₂: the sum of the three principal 2×2 minors
content: The second elementary symmetric function of a $3\times3$ matrix is defined combinatorially as the sum of the three principal $2\times2$ minors: $e_2(A) = (A_{00}A_{11} - A_{01}A_{10}) + (A_{00}A_{22} - A_{02}A_{20}) + (A_{11}A_{22} - A_{12}A_{21})$. For a matrix with eigenvalues $a, b, c$ this equals $ab + ac + bc$. Defining $e_2$ purely from the entries (no eigenvalues) is what lets the matrix-side identity below hold over an arbitrary commutative ring.
mathContext: $e_2(A) = \sum_{\text{principal } 2\times2} \det = ab + ac + bc$ on the spectrum.

title: The matrix-side Newton identity over any commutative ring
content: `trace_cube_fin_three` proves $\operatorname{tr}(A^3) = (\operatorname{tr}A)^3 - 3(\operatorname{tr}A)\,e_2(A) + 3\det A$ as a polynomial identity in the nine entries — valid over $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Q}$, or any commutative ring, with no field, no algebraic closure, and no eigenvalues. The proof is pure computation: `simp only` expands $(A^3).\text{trace}$, $A.\text{trace}$, $e_2(A)$, and $A.\det$ via `trace_fin_three`, `det_fin_three`, `mul_apply`, and `Fin.sum_univ_three`, after which `ring` discharges the resulting identity in the entries. This is the ring-universal heart of the result; eigenvalues enter only later.

title: e₂ wears two hats: minor sum and charpoly coefficient
content: `charpoly_fin_three` expands the characteristic polynomial $\det(X\cdot I - A)$ entrywise (via `charmatrix` and `det_fin_three`, normalised by `ring`) into elementary-symmetric form $X^3 - (\operatorname{tr}A)X^2 + e_2(A)X - \det A$. `charpoly_coeff_one_eq_e2` then reads off the $X^1$-coefficient: $\chi_A.\text{coeff}\,1 = e_2(A)$. This double identity — $e_2$ defined combinatorially as the minor sum, but appearing as a charpoly coefficient — is the crucial bridge: by Vieta the $X^1$-coefficient is the second elementary symmetric function $ab+ac+bc$ of the eigenvalues, which is exactly what turns the matrix-side identity into a spectral one.

title: The spectral upgrade: algebraic closure enters only here
content: `trace_cube_eq_sum_cube_eigenvalues` lifts the matrix-side identity to the genuinely spectral $\operatorname{tr}(A^3) = \lambda_1^3 + \lambda_2^3 + \lambda_3^3$ over an algebraically closed field. Algebraic closure is needed only now, to split the characteristic polynomial. `card_eigenvalues_fin_three` (from the parent's `card_eigenvalues_eq_dim`) gives the eigenvalue multiset exactly three elements $\{a,b,c\}$; Vieta (`charpoly_eq_prod_eigenvalues`) then identifies the three symmetric functions with $\operatorname{tr}A = a+b+c$ and $\det A = abc$ (inherited from the parent) and $e_2(A) = ab+ac+bc$ (from `charpoly_coeff_one_eq_e2` plus the explicit cubic factorisation). Substituting into `trace_cube_fin_three` and matching against the three-variable identity $a^3+b^3+c^3 = (a+b+c)^3 - 3(a+b+c)(ab+ac+bc) + 3abc$ closes it by `ring`.

title: A trace power sum of an unknowable spectrum
content: `trace_cube_example` instantiates the matrix-side identity at the rational matrix $\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2&0\\0&3&1\\4&0&2\end{psmallmatrix}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Its eigenvalues are not rational, yet $\operatorname{tr}(A^3)$ is completely forced by $\operatorname{tr}A = 6$, the minor sum $e_2(A)$, and $\det A$ — read off without ever solving the cubic. The trailing `#print axioms` calls audit the three headline theorems and confirm they depend only on the foundational `propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound`; there is no `native_decide` (no `Lean.ofReduceBool`) and no `sorryAx`, consistent with the entry's 0-axiom claim.
